deferred.question: claude keeps saying "I'll use the tool" in text before actually calling it, can I suppress that
what_the_corpus_does_say: 'Prompting best practices' has an 'Eliminating preambles' accordion: prefills were used to skip introductory text, and the migration is to instruct directly in the system prompt ('Respond directly without preamble...'), or use XML tags, structured outputs, or tool calling, and strip anything remaining in post-processing.
'Handle tool calls' shows an example response in which a text block ('I'll check the current weather in San Francisco for you.') precedes the tool_use block, documenting that the behaviour occurs.
deferred.what_the_corpus_does_not_say: Nothing connects the two. The preamble guidance is scoped to response preambles generally and arrived via prefill migration; it never addresses text emitted alongside a tool_use block, and 'preamble' is absent from every tool-use document checked (Tool use with Claude, Parallel tool use, Troubleshooting tool use, How tool use works).
deferred.why_deferred: Admitting it means citing general preamble guidance for a tool-use question the corpus never scopes it to. Rejecting it means calling a question unsupported when a directly applicable instruction does exist. Either verdict is a judgement the coordinator should make, not one to bury in a packet.

dedup_rule.detect: after all 150 are adjudicated, group SUPPORTED cases by their gold span set; any group of size > 1 is an evidence collision
dedup_rule.adjudicate: each collision gets an explicit ruling — keep one, keep both because the reasoning types genuinely differ, or reject both
dedup_rule.do_not: do not resolve collisions by looking at how any retrieval system scores the cases
dedup_rule.record: every ruling is written down with its reason before the accepted 100 are frozen

yield.caveat: Not a forecast. Slice A is over-represented in what has been adjudicated; a real rate follows when slice A closes.
